cache_policy.capabilities: exact capability set; payload text included in retained-key weight
cache_policy.key: Exact typed JSON structural content with exact number text, ordered nodes/edges and schema versions; not Gson JsonElement.equals or hash-only equality.
cache_policy.eligibility: Canonical native definitions and explicitly audited immutable configuration classes only. Unknown extension/custom definition, mutable Number, or mutable configuration bypasses the cache.
cache_policy.lifecycle: server stopped, client logout, and client stopped hooks clear cache; per-player server logout does not clear every player cache.
cache_policy.limits: Conservative key/result weight budget, not a measurement of total retained JVM heap. No VM execution data cache and no manager permission/budget/order change.

interpretation: The definition-with-migration measurements after warmup exercise repeated unchanged eligible successful graphs and a retained cache entry. They are cache-hit measurements, not cold compilation speedups.

Direct compiler cases remain uncached and are retained as a control. Dense128 direct compiler P50 allocation rises from 1088688 to 1100544 bytes in this run, so a universal allocation reduction is not claimed.
Profile capture is a separate 128-request pass: dense128 definition retains 128 migrations but actual compilations and both decode counters fall from 128/16384/16384 to 0/0/0 with 128 hits.

Misses, evictions, unsafe mutable/extension configurations and changed capabilities/configuration graphs are covered by meaningful contract/concurrency/budget tests; the benchmark is not a world action runtime test.

measurement_scope.limitations: single-server-thread microbenchmark; not multiplayer TPS or PVP-player load measurement

interpretation: Entity ordering now computes UUID text once per candidate within a single query; it retains ordering and does not cache world query results between actions.

The structure query algorithms were not optimized. Their differences, including the 4096-cell allocation reduction, are observed results with unisolated JIT/escape-analysis/startup effects as possible explanations, not established causes.

Run 1 entities_64 P99 regressed; structure_distance_sparse P95/P99, structure_contents_stale P99, and summary_budget_reject P99 also rose. One 128-sample run does not establish general tail latency or multiplayer TPS improvement.
The independent optimized replicate is retained in full; neither optimized run is selected as a best result.

Replicate r2: entities_1024 P95/P99 are 298.0/510.9 microseconds versus baseline 282.0/403.0, entities_64 P95 is 84.1 versus 69.4 microseconds; structure_distance_sparse and summary_budget_reject P99 also regress. Entity allocation reductions repeat; general tail latency improvement is not claimed.

Replicate r2 structure_contents_sparse4096 allocation P50 is 166648 bytes, exactly baseline, while run 1 was 68344. This unmodified structure path variation is retained as noise/measurement context, not credited as an algorithm improvement.

real_render_profiler_disabled.surface_elapsed_scope: EditorSurface.renderInternal wall elapsed only; excludes extractRenderState configuration sync, tooltip surface and explicit present. It is not a thread CPU or GPU-completion measurement.
real_render_profiler_disabled.render_event_scope: Local Minecraft.renderFrame fires Pre immediately before GameRenderer.render and Post immediately after it. Window texture acquisition, update/extract happen before Pre; blit, command submission, surface.present and frame limiter happen after Post. Academy ScreenDispatcher performs editor command generation at ScreenEvent.Render.Pre during GUI extraction before this interval, so the separate editor-surface measurements are not nested inside this event timer. Listener work and waits inside render may contribute. This is not a full frame interval or GPU timestamp.

visual_review.historical_graph_provenance: Reconstructed historical 10-node topology, not an imported original user save.
known_findings: No historical background/glyph loss reproduced in the reviewed reconstructed 10-node scenes; this does not establish that the original saved-graph defect is fixed.
At the same 65% zoom, arithmetic multi-line configuration text is crowded/overlapping in both baseline and optimized 128-node scenes; low-zoom readability remains open.

Baseline 32-node after-resource-language screenshot captured the Mojang reload overlay; it is not accepted as a view of the editor. Optimized fixture waits for the overlay to disappear for 10 ticks before its replacement screenshot.
visual_review.review_result: Accepted within recorded limits: reconstructed legacy ten-node views complete, resource-reload replacement editor view restored, visible 128-node content complete; low-zoom configuration text crowding remains.

measurement_limits: Reflection microbenchmarks include cached Method.invoke overhead and do not predict whole-frame time
nanoTime surface/event timings are wall elapsed and may include waits inside their scopes; ThreadMXBean render-event CPU is reported separately when supported
RenderFrame Pre/Post encloses GameRenderer.render only in the local patched Minecraft; acquisition/extract and explicit submit/present/frame limiter are outside, and GPU completion is not measured
Synthetic editor capabilities are not learned-player or runtime admission acceptance
The historical ten-node topology is reconstructed; pixel review is required before closing the old glyph/background defect
1200 ticks is the default soak; 12000 ticks must be explicitly selected for the independent ten-minute run
RenderFrame event statistics exclude the Academy extract/surface command construction work; surface elapsed and rebuild counters are reported separately.
The thread-allocation key was renamed from render_thread_allocated_bytes_per_frame to render_event_thread_allocated_bytes without changing the sampling boundary.
Thread CPU clock samples are quantized (often 0 or 15.625 ms); a zero median is not zero CPU cost.

Observed frame counts differ by scene and run (including baseline128 123 vs optimized128 180). These are real capture windows and surface timing does not imply equal FPS, whole-frame time or GPU improvement.
Zero schema/node/palette/validation rebuild counters describe the warmed steady-state window only.
Baseline historical soak is 1200 client ticks; optimized soak is explicitly 12000 ticks. Those soak durations are not a matched latency comparison.
No viewport culling implementation is included; zero culled counters are not evidence of culling optimization.

frame_limiter_context.interpretation: Both runs retained the afk inactivity limiter. The later 128-node window can be limited after the 60-second inactivity threshold, consistent with its lower observed frame count. This fixture is not a fixed-120-FPS throughput benchmark; surface and RenderFrame event timing exclude the external frame limiter. This is context, not an isolated causal measurement.
frame_limiter_context.future_actual_frame_rate_measurement: Explicitly fix and record AFK/inactivity configuration in a separate future benchmark; do not rewrite this preserved baseline.

pre_validation_review_hardening: Strict cache key handles parsed numeric Gson equality/hash collisions (9007199254740992 vs 9007199254740993), signed zero and mutable Number conservatively.
Enum constant-specific runtime subclasses are audited through final immutable instance fields; stateless ScalarKind overrides are supported and mutable subclass fields rejected.
Extra capability Identifier text is included in bounded retained-key weight; oversize entries bypass.
Unknown extension/custom definition/configuration states bypass compilation and UI caches; no arbitrary Object/package-name/record-shape assumptions.

Actual NeoForge subscriber scanner/bus handling for package-private lifecycle class was checked before final builds. Runtime lifecycle subscriber registration was observed by root in optimized client log.
limitations: Timing/allocation samples are from one machine/JVM and instrumented real client/server fixtures; thread allocation excludes other threads/native memory and profiler capture is separate from timing.
Compile graphs are valid ordinary native graphs; compilation/codec validation does not execute the action graph or grant runtime permissions.
Compiler permission, migration, extension and manager budgets remain semantically guarded; cache eviction is conservative weight budgeting, not a full heap bound measurement.
The final report closes the measured three-domain loop only, and preserves observed regressions and visual defects.
